title: Maximum Width Ramp
statement: Call a pair of indices `(i, j)` of the integer array `nums` a *ramp* when `i < j` and `nums[i] <= nums[j]`; its width is `j - i`. Return the largest width over all ramps in `nums`, or `0` when `nums` contains no ramp at all.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every pair `(i, j)` is O(n²). Notice that a left end `i` is only worth considering if no earlier index holds a value that is smaller or equal, because that earlier index would give a wider ramp to the same `j`. Those useful left ends form a strictly decreasing run of values, which fits a stack. Then scanning `j` from the right, each candidate left end can be matched with the farthest `j` that reaches it and discarded.

## Approach

1. Walk left to right and push index `i` onto `stack` whenever `nums[i]` is smaller than the value at the top; the stack holds the strictly decreasing prefix minima.
2. Walk `j` from the last index down to 0.
3. While the top of the stack has a value `<= nums[j]`, pop it as `i` and update `best` with `j - i`. No later (smaller) `j` could give that `i` a wider ramp, so popping is safe.
4. Return `best`, which stays `0` when no ramp exists.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [6, 0, 8, 2, 1, 5]`. The first pass pushes index 0 (value 6) and index 1 (value 0); nothing later is below 0, so `stack = [0, 1]`. Scanning back, `j = 5` (value 5) pops index 1 (value 0) for width 4, then stops at value 6. `j = 4, 3` cannot reach 6. `j = 2` (value 8) pops index 0 for width 2. The answer is `best = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is pushed at most once and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack in the worst case (a strictly falling array).

## Pitfalls

- Push only strictly smaller values; pushing equal values just adds candidates that can never be wider.
- Scan `j` from the right so the first match for each left end is its widest one.
- The condition is `<=`, not `<`: equal values form a valid ramp.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | indices of the strictly decreasing prefix minima, smallest value on top |
| `i` | a left end index taken from the stack |
| `j` | the right end index, scanned from the end |
| `best` | widest ramp found so far |

narration.2: The stack will hold the only indices worth using as a ramp's left end.
narration.3: Scan every index from left to right.
narration.4: A new left end is useful only if its value is smaller than every value before it.
narration.5: Push it; the values on the stack keep strictly decreasing.
narration.9: No ramp found yet, so the best width starts at 0.
narration.10: Try right ends from the far end of the array towards the start.
narration.11: While the smallest remaining left end fits under nums[j], this j is its widest partner.
narration.12: Take that left end off the stack; no smaller j could beat this width for it.
narration.13: Record the width j - i if it is the widest so far.
narration.16: Every candidate left end was matched as far right as possible; return the widest ramp.
